accepted.s: The 121st Report of the Law Commission of India dealt with which of the following subjects?
accepted.x: The 121st Report, published in 1987, dealt with the National Judicial Service Commission.
accepted.tq: Match the report number with its precise subject.
accepted.sec: Law Commission reports → report number + subject

accepted.s: The 170th Report of the Law Commission of India recommended which of the following electoral reforms?
o: Increasing Lok Sabha strength by 25 per cent through a party-list system
Simultaneous elections to Parliament and State Legislatures
De-registration of parties that do not contest elections for ten years
accepted.x: The 170th Report, submitted in 1999, recommended raising the strength of the Lok Sabha by 25 per cent through a party-list arrangement.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive recommendation to identify the report.
accepted.sec: Law Commission reports → report number + subject

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: 214th Report — Review of the procedure for appointing judges
279th Report — Draft model Bilateral Investment Treaty
accepted.x: The 214th Report, submitted in 2008, reviewed the procedure for appointing judges. The other subjects belong to different reports or are not stated for those report numbers.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure report–subject pair and eliminate swapped subjects.
accepted.sec: Law Commission reports → report number + subject

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. 14th Report — Reform of judicial administration
b. 59th Report — Family courts
c. 114th Report — Gram Nyayalayas
d. 230th Report — “Uncle judge” syndrome in High Courts
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The 14th, 59th, 114th and 230th Reports dealt respectively with judicial administration, family courts, Gram Nyayalayas and the “Uncle judge” syndrome.
accepted.tq: Check each report–subject pair independently before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Law Commission reports → report number + subject

accepted.s: The 255th Report of the Law Commission of India, submitted in 2015, recommended which of the following?
o: A constitutional amendment establishing a National Judicial Service Commission
A single regulator for higher education
EVM totalisers and de-registration of parties that skip elections for ten years
accepted.x: The 255th Report dealt with electoral reforms, including EVM totalisers and de-registration of parties that do not contest elections for ten years.
accepted.tq: Identify the report through its paired electoral-reform recommendations.
accepted.sec: Law Commission reports → report number + subject

accepted.s: The 279th Report of the Law Commission recommended that sedition should be:
o: Applied only during a national emergency
accepted.x: The 279th Report, submitted in 2023, recommended retaining sedition with safeguards.
accepted.tq: Distinguish retention with safeguards from complete repeal or unrestricted use.
accepted.sec: Law Commission reports → report number + subject

accepted.s: What was the position taken in the 2018 Consultation Paper of the 21st Law Commission on a Uniform Civil Code?
o: It was neither necessary nor desirable at that stage
It was desirable only for personal laws of minorities
It was constitutionally compulsory and immediately implementable
It was declared outside the scope of the Law Commission
accepted.x: The 2018 Consultation Paper stated that a Uniform Civil Code was “neither necessary nor desirable at this stage.”
accepted.tq: Test the exact official formulation rather than a broader paraphrase.
accepted.sec: Law Commission reports → report number + subject

accepted.s:
With reference to the Law Commission of India, consider the following statements:
1. It is an executive body established by a Government of India order for a fixed three-year term.
2. It is an advisory body and not a quasi-judicial body.
3. It submits its reports to the President of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Commission reports to the Ministry of Law and Justice, not to the President, making statement 3 false.
accepted.tq: Check the body’s legal status and reporting authority separately.
accepted.sec: Law Commission reports → report number + subject

accepted.s: Who chaired the first Law Commission established after India’s Independence?
accepted.x: The first post-Independence Law Commission was established in 1955 and was chaired by M.C. Setalvad.
accepted.tq: Use the historical chairperson rather than confusing the colonial precursor with the post-Independence body.
accepted.sec: Law Commission reports → report number + subject

accepted.s: The colonial Law Commission associated with the production of the Indian Penal Code was chaired by:
accepted.x: Macaulay’s Law Commission was the colonial precursor and produced the Indian Penal Code in 1860.
accepted.tq: Separate the colonial precursor from the first post-Independence Law Commission.
accepted.sec: Law Commission reports → report number + subject

accepted.s: The Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 was formed primarily to examine:
accepted.x: The JPC chaired by P.P. Chaudhary examined the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, concerning simultaneous elections. The Bill was introduced on 17 December 2024.
accepted.tq: Link the committee’s subject with the Bill under examination.
accepted.sec: Parliamentary committees - JPC formed, subject, chairperson

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: JPC on Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill — D. Purandeswari
JPC on VBSA Bill, 2025 — P.P. Chaudhary
JPC on VBSA Bill, 2025 — D. Purandeswari
accepted.x: D. Purandeswari chaired the 31-member JPC on the VBSA Bill, 2025, which concerned a single higher-education regulator.
accepted.tq: Use chairperson–committee matching and reject swapped names.
accepted.sec: Parliamentary committees - JPC formed, subject, chairperson

accepted.s: The Public Accounts Committee for 2026–27 is chaired by:
accepted.x: K.C. Venugopal is the chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee for 2026–27, which examines CAG audit reports.
accepted.tq: Identify the chairperson through the committee’s current year and subject.
accepted.sec: Parliamentary committees - JPC formed, subject, chairperson

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Public Accounts Committee:
1. It was set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1919.
2. It consists of 22 members, including 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.
3. A Minister can be a member of the Committee.
4. It has been chaired by a member of the Opposition since 1967.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. A Minister cannot be a member of the Public Accounts Committee, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the exception in the committee’s composition and chairpersonship rules.
accepted.sec: Parliamentary committees - JPC formed, subject, chairperson

accepted.s: The National Crime Records Bureau was established in 1986 by:
o: A resolution of the United Nations
An Act of Parliament following the Sarkaria Commission
An executive order following the Tandon Committee
accepted.x: The NCRB was set up in 1986 by executive order after the Tandon Committee. It functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an executive creation from a statutory or constitutional body.

accepted.s: Which organisation publishes the report ‘Crime in India’?

accepted.s: According to Crime in India 2024, which State recorded the highest number of human-trafficking cases?

accepted.tq: Match the current appointment with the correct institution.

accepted.s: The Periodic Labour Force Survey is conducted by the:
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
accepted.x: PLFS is conducted by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation; it has been released monthly since 2025.
accepted.tq: Match the survey with its conducting agency and ministry.
accepted.sec: Survey reports → conducting agency

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NFHS — MoHFW, with IIPS Mumbai as nodal institution
accepted.x: NFHS is conducted under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, with the International Institute for Population Sciences, Mumbai, as the nodal institution.
accepted.tq: Begin with the known survey–agency pair and eliminate cross-swapped agencies.
accepted.sec: Survey reports → conducting agency

accepted.s: The Annual Status of Education Report is conducted by:
accepted.x: ASER is conducted by Pratham, a non-governmental organisation.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the NGO-led survey from government surveys.
accepted.sec: Survey reports → conducting agency

accepted.s: The Household Consumption Expenditure Survey for 2022–23 and 2023–24 is published by the:
accepted.x: HCES 2022–23 and 2023–24 are conducted by the NSO under MoSPI and provide weights for the new CPI introduced in 2024.
accepted.tq: Link the survey to both its agency and its stated statistical use.
accepted.sec: Survey reports → conducting agency

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding AISHE is correct?
o: It is conducted by Pratham and measures household consumption.
It is conducted by the Ministry of Education, and the 2022–23 and 2023–24 editions were released together in July 2026.
It is conducted by the Registrar General of India as part of the Census.
It is conducted by NITI Aayog to prepare the SDG Index.
accepted.x: AISHE is conducted by the Ministry of Education. The 2022–23 and 2023–24 reports were released together in July 2026, when undergraduate enrolment fell for the first time.
accepted.tq: Use the conducting ministry and release detail to reject familiar agency swaps.
accepted.sec: Survey reports → conducting agency

accepted.s: The Sample Registration System 2024 is associated with which agency?
accepted.x: SRS 2024 is associated with the Registrar General of India.
accepted.tq: Match the demographic survey with the registration authority.
accepted.sec: Survey reports → conducting agency

accepted.s: Census 2027 is being conducted by the:
o: Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs
NITI Aayog under the Cabinet Secretariat
accepted.x: Census 2027 is being conducted by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs. It is the first digital Census, with houselisting in 2026.
accepted.tq: Identify the statutory census authority rather than a general statistical agency.
accepted.sec: Survey reports → conducting agency

accepted.s: Which organisation publishes the Export Preparedness Index?
o: Ministry of Commerce and Industry alone
accepted.x: The Export Preparedness Index 2024, its fourth edition, is published by NITI Aayog.
accepted.tq: Match the index with its central publishing agency.

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to the Export Preparedness Index 2024:
1. Maharashtra — first among large States
2. Tamil Nadu — second among large States
3. Gujarat — third among large States
4. Andhra Pradesh — fifth among large States
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
accepted.x: The stated order among large States is Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh. Therefore all four pairs are correct.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Fiscal Health Index 2026?
o: Arunachal Pradesh — last among North-Eastern and Himalayan States
Andhra Pradesh — first among major States
accepted.x: Odisha ranked first among major States in the Fiscal Health Index 2026, while Punjab ranked last. Arunachal Pradesh ranked first among North-Eastern and Himalayan States, and Andhra Pradesh ranked 17th.

accepted.s: Which of the following indices is published by NITI Aayog?
accepted.x: The SDG India Index, Composite Water Management Index, School Education Quality Index and Health Index are associated with NITI Aayog. The Good Governance Index is associated with DARPG.

accepted.x: The Good Governance Index is published by DARPG and includes sectors such as grievance redressal and e-governance.

accepted.s:
With reference to the 2019 amendment concerning the National Human Rights Commission, consider the following statements:
1. An SC judge, and not only a former Chief Justice of India, can be appointed as its chairperson.
2. The chairperson’s term is three years or until attaining the age of 70 years.
3. The chairpersons of the NCBC and NCPCR are deemed members of the NHRC.
4. The Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities is deemed a member of the NHRC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The 2019 amendment broadened eligibility for the NHRC chairperson and included the specified commission chairpersons and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities as deemed members.
accepted.tq: Check each statutory amendment detail instead of assuming the earlier composition continues.
accepted.sec: Commission chairpersons and members newly appointed
